samples.summary: `api-keys revoke` echoes the backend's full API-key row (including `hashedKey`) to stdout, and this change removes the last client-side way to suppress it
samples.evidence: `ApiKeyService.revoke` (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.service.ts:58-63) returns `prisma.apiKey.update(...)` with no `select`, so the response body carries every column of the row — `hashedKey` (the sha256 the auth path looks the key up by in `validateKey`, api-key.service.ts:66-70), `prefix`, `createdBy`, etc. The CLI prints that body verbatim: `output(res.data, opts.format)` at packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:47. Before this diff `--quiet` short-circuited `output()` (formatter.ts, removed `if (quiet) return`), so `wafflebase api-keys revoke <id> --quiet` in a CI job emitted nothing; after the change the stored key hash is written to stdout unconditionally and lands in shared build logs. It is not directly usable to authenticate (validateKey hashes the presented raw key), which caps impact, but it is stored credential material the CLI has no reason to display. Fix belongs on the backend response shape (add a `select`) or on the CLI redacting the field.

samples.summary: Removing `--quiet` suppression makes every result body unconditionally reach stdout, regressing any workflow that used `--quiet` to keep document/cell contents out of shared logs
samples.evidence: `output()` now always calls `console.log(format(data, fmt))` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:26-28) and every call site dropped its `opts.quiet` argument (e.g. docs.ts:83, cells.ts:26, notes.ts:43, slides.ts:48). Previously `--quiet` was documented as 'Suppress output' (root.ts, old flag help; packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:109), so an operator running `wafflebase sheets cells get <doc> --quiet` or `docs content <doc> --quiet` inside a CI step got zero bytes; now the full document/cell payload is printed into the job log. The behavior change is intentional and matches docs/design/cli.md §9, but it is a confidentiality-relevant behavior change for existing callers and the README/design edits do not call out that `>/dev/null` is now the only suppression. Worth an explicit note in the release/migration text rather than a code change.

samples.summary: `--format table`/`csv` print server- and collaborator-controlled strings to the terminal with no control-character sanitization; the change makes that output unsuppressible
samples.evidence: `formatTable` interpolates values with `String(row[k] ?? '')` and joins them (packages/cli/src/output/table.ts:13-23); `formatCsv` likewise. `output()` writes the result straight to the TTY (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:27). Cell values, document titles and note content are writable by any collaborator in the workspace, so a value containing ANSI/OSC escapes (e.g. `]0;...` or cursor/clear sequences) manipulates the terminal of anyone running `wafflebase docs list --format table` or `sheets cells get --format csv`. The default `json` format is safe because `JSON.stringify` escapes every code point below U+0020, and the error envelope in `outputError` (formatter.ts:54-56) goes through `JSON.stringify` too. This is pre-existing, but the diff widens the reachable surface by removing the `--quiet` early return that previously discarded these bodies. Mitigation: strip C0/C1 and OSC sequences in the table/csv formatters.

samples.summary: No redaction layer on the now-always-emitted error envelope; server-supplied message text is forwarded verbatim
samples.evidence: `outputError` unconditionally prints `error.message` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:52-57) and callers feed it server-controlled text — e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:41-42 throws `new Error(res.data.error.message)` built from the API response. I traced every `throw new Error` in packages/cli/src (grep for `throw new`) and none interpolates the API key, access token or refresh token, and `HttpClient` never puts credentials in a thrown message (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:96-141), so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence low impact. Flagging only that nothing guards this path now that `--quiet` no longer gates it: any future error message that embeds config (server URL with a token, session path contents) will be printed on stderr even in the mode users assume is silent. A small allowlist/redaction in `outputError`, or a test asserting the envelope never contains `config.apiKey`/`accessToken`, would close it.
